justification: Reads the user's media files from shared storage on API 32 and below, where the granular READ_MEDIA_* permissions do not exist yet; the Wear store variant strips it because media access sits outside its Play boundary (S3178).
Writes sorted, copied and captured files to shared storage on API 28 and below, and is capped with maxSdkVersion 28 so no newer system is ever asked for it.
Lists and opens the user's photos on API 33+, where this granular permission replaces the blanket storage read for images.
Lists and opens the user's videos on API 33+, where this granular permission replaces the blanket storage read for video.
Lists and plays the user's music and voice notes on API 33+, where this granular permission replaces the blanket storage read for audio.
Lets the sorter delete and move media files directly on Android 12+ without a system confirmation dialog in front of every single item, which is the whole point of a fast sorting pass.

Powers the in-app camera capture surfaces and, where the broadcast source ships, the live camera broadcast; the accompanying camera feature is declared required=false so Play keeps the build visible on camera-less devices (S3155).

Serves three consumer families - opt-in GPS geotagging of in-app camera photos (S0766), the launcher compass, speed, altitude and map gadgets (S1179/S1175), and the Network Monitor GNSS section (S1433) - plus the watch's Tourist dashboard, which is a GPS instrument (S3115).
The approximate half of the same location grant, declared because Android 12+ offers the user the coarse choice and every one of those screens stays usable on whichever fix it is given.

S1454: the only seam onto ContactsContract is ContactSnapshotDataSource, reached solely from the launcher source set, so every flavor that does not mount the launcher removes the permission rather than leaving it declared and unusable.
Reaches the remote sources the app is built around - SMB, FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, cloud providers and internet streams; the Wear store variant declares none of it (S3178).
Android 37's explicit local-network grant, needed to reach SMB, FTP and SFTP shares on the LAN; S0448 drops it from lite, which is local-files-only.
Tells the app whether a transport is up before it opens a share, a cloud folder or a stream, so a dead connection is reported instead of hanging.
Reads the current Wi-Fi link for the Network Monitor's Wi-Fi section and, on the watch, for the mini-program that samples this device's own radios (S1710).
S1013: receives multicast (mDNS/NSD) so the app can discover companion _sftp-fms._tcp servers on the local network.

Keeps the CPU awake during background playback, long file operations and WorkManager foreground work; the declaration also removes the API 25 cap a debug library contributes, without which WorkManager.startForeground throws a SecurityException on API 26+.
Haptic feedback - the Wear sync confirmation on the phone and the watch's own tactile responses, where a buzz is often the only signal the wrist gets.

The untyped foreground-service permission the platform checks below API 34 for background audio playback, voice recording and scheduled operations; the Wear store variant removes it because every foreground service it could cover belongs to an excluded category (S3178).

Media3 unconditionally calls startForeground with the mediaPlayback type on any playback start from API 34, so removing this permission crashes background audio on Android 14+ (recorded in the release overlay's own note).

S1862: on API 33+ even a foreground-service notification is hidden without this grant, so playback, recording, screen-capture and scheduled-operation notices would run with nothing on screen to say so.

Records voice notes (S0100/S0349), the audio track of in-app camera video, and the microphone track of screen video recording (S0774); S1442 drops it from photos, which reaches no microphone path at all.
Reschedules scheduled file operations and re-posts the flashlight shade shortcut after a reboot; the release build type removes it until the scheduled-operations feature is submitted for Play review.
Types the WorkManager foreground service that runs scheduled file operations on API 34+; the release build type removes it until that feature is submitted for Play review.

S0349/S1862: the API 34 microphone foreground-service type for the Quick Audio Recorder widget and the watch's voice recorder, which own the microphone session outside any screen so a dropped wrist cannot end a recording.
S2386: expands and collapses the notification shade and quick-settings panels from the app's own surfaces without requiring an accessibility service.
Asks the user to exempt the app from battery optimisation so scheduled file operations still fire on time; the release build type removes it until that feature is submitted for Play review.

S3154: only the sideload build keeps the camera on air after the app leaves the screen, and Google Play requires a declared background-camera use case for this permission, so the store flavors ship the same service without it.

S1415: requested at run time and only when the launcher tray is about to show a SIM indicator, a refusal simply leaving both slots absent; S2726 removes the merger-implied copy from the flavors that never mount the launcher.

S2576: the launcher's app-action uninstall row hands ACTION_DELETE to the system uninstaller, whose confirmation screen closes itself silently for an app targeting API 28+ that does not hold this permission.
S1441: RadioControlContractImpl calls WifiManager.setWifiEnabled when the user taps the launcher's Wi-Fi tile, so the declaration ships together with the code that uses it.

The Network Monitor's Bluetooth section on API 30 and below, where adapter control still runs through the legacy admin permission; API 31+ routes through BLUETOOTH_CONNECT instead, so this one is capped at maxSdkVersion 30.

S1515: the read half of the legacy Bluetooth pair - on API 30 and below the adapter state and bonded-device count are guarded by this install-time permission, which has no request dialog, so an undeclared build reported no permission for ever.

Reads the current Wi-Fi connection details and the visible-network list on API 33+; the watch declares it with neverForLocation so the scan runs without a location grant Play would review against the store description.
The Bluetooth section's adapter state and bonded-device names on API 31+, where it replaces the legacy BLUETOOTH pair above.

S2012: all-files access is a sideload-only capability - Google Play refused two updates over it as not a core feature - so only this overlay declares it, and StoragePermissionRule reads the merged manifest to decide whether the direct filesystem path is offered at all.
S0183: installs an APK straight from the Browse screen, a sideload-only capability that is forbidden in market builds.

S0621/S0630: draws the persistent edge handle the user swipes to start a screen capture over other apps; on standard it is injected only while the fms.edgeGestureOverlay build flag is on, so a Play-fast release can ship without it.

S0621/S0630: types OverlayHostService, the foreground service that hosts the edge screen-capture strip, for which the platform offers no better category; it travels with the overlay and is injected into standard under the same build flag.

S1614/S2458: feeds the launcher's step gadget and the watch's step counter and detector; Play classifies it as a health feature and blocks the release commit until the Health declaration is answered, a review surface the sideload flavor does not have.

S0559: types the MediaProjection screenshot and screen-recording services, the Play-safe confirmable capture path shared by the store and sideload builds; on standard it arrives only while the fms.screenCapture build flag is on.
S0249: Quest hand tracking for the immersive OpenXR surfaces, paired with an optional oculus.software.handtracking feature so the single-APK strategy keeps phone visibility on Play.

S2457: reads the heart rate on watches running API 30 to 35, where the granular health permission does not exist yet; it is capped at maxSdkVersion 35 rather than removed because such a watch has no other way to ask, and background access is deliberately out of scope.
S2457: the API 36 granular health permission that replaces BODY_SENSORS for the same heart-rate measurement, which exists only while its screen is open.
S1728: asks the platform for a wide-band transport while a stream plays on the watch and gives it back when the stream ends; only the request needs this, reading the current link does not.
S2941: lets the listen-request notification open ListenRequestActivity by itself, putting the app in the foreground so the microphone foreground service may start without the user tapping anything.
Receives the macrobenchmark harness's PREPARE_APP broadcast, which arrives from another uid, so it must be exported; it is declared in the benchmark build type only and reaches no shipped build.
Opens a named benchmark journey on request from the macrobenchmark harness, which is another process; it is declared in the benchmark build type only and reaches no shipped build.

S2818: the Quick Settings tile that starts a live broadcast; a tile service is bound by the system, so it must be exported, and it is guarded by BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE so only the system may bind it.
S2818: the home-screen widget that starts a live broadcast; an AppWidget provider receives APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher and the system, which requires an exported receiver.
S1986: opens the camera host in a named mode for the host-side WYSIWYG sweep, exported on purpose because the sender is adb shell am broadcast, which is another uid; debug build type only.

S2380: sets a colour theme on the running process for the host-side UI sweep, exported for the same reason as its sibling because a non-exported receiver is skipped for an adb-issued broadcast; debug build type only.

S0404: the home-screen activity the system offers as a launcher, so it carries a HOME intent filter and the system must be able to start it; it ships disabled and is enabled only when the user turns launcher mode on.

S1205: receives ACTION_CONFIRM_PIN_SHORTCUT, which the system delivers only to the launcher currently holding the home role, so it is inert until that role is ours and needs no enable lever of its own.
S0404: the share-sheet entry that pins a place sent as plain text from another app; a SEND target must be exported to appear in the system chooser, and the alias ships disabled.
The app's launcher entry point, exported so the home screen, the Android TV grid and the app shortcuts can start it.
The folder browse screen, exported so home-screen shortcuts and widgets can open a specific resource straight into it.
Handles a shared broadcast file or an fmsbcast link handed over by another app, so it must be reachable from outside the process.
The in-app media player, exported so shortcuts and widgets can open a media item directly into playback.
The settings screen, exported so launcher shortcuts and settings deep links can open it directly.
Hosts the Google Drive folder picker and must be reachable by the external sign-in flow that returns into it; the FOSS flavor removes it because no Google auth SDK is on its classpath (S0403).
Hosts the Dropbox folder picker and must be reachable by the external sign-in flow that returns into it; the FOSS flavor removes it because the Dropbox SDK is off its classpath (S0403).
Hosts the OneDrive folder picker and must be reachable by the external sign-in flow that returns into it; the FOSS flavor removes it because MSAL is off its classpath (S0403).

AppAuth's OAuth redirect receiver for browser-based Google Drive sign-in on Quest and other devices without Google Play Services; the browser hands the custom-scheme redirect back to it, which requires an exported activity.

The Dropbox SDK's own sign-in activity, which the Dropbox app or the browser returns to over the db-appKey scheme; the flavors without cloud support remove it so two installed builds cannot both claim that scheme and trip the SDK's security alert.
S0232: MSAL's browser-tab receiver for OneDrive sign-in; every signing keystore that can produce a cloud-enabled build needs its own msauth redirect filter here, or MSAL refuses the flow outright.
The configuration screen the launcher starts with APPWIDGET_CONFIGURE when a resource-launch widget is dropped on the home screen, which requires an exported activity.
The configuration screen the launcher starts with APPWIDGET_CONFIGURE when a random photo frame widget is added, which requires an exported activity.
The favourites home-screen widget; an AppWidget provider receives APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher and the system, which requires an exported receiver.
S0353: the scheduled-tasks widget with its run-all and pause buttons; it receives APPWIDGET_UPDATE and its own action broadcasts from the launcher, which requires an exported receiver.
A Media3 MediaSessionService, bound from outside the process by the system media controls, Bluetooth headsets and Android Auto, which is why the session service must be exported.
The Quick Settings tile for audio play and pause; a tile service is bound by the system and is guarded by BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE, and the photos flavor removes it because it ships no audio support.
S0683: the Quick Settings tile that opens the Quick Launch Panel as a second entry point beside the left-edge gesture; bound by the system and guarded by BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE.
The widget that opens a configured resource from the home screen; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE.
S1916: the widget that launches a saved stream; present wherever stream support is, and removed in lite, photos and FOSS where SUPPORT_STREAMS is false so their widget pickers never offer it.
S1916: the APPWIDGET_CONFIGURE screen for the stream launch widget, started by the launcher and removed together with its widget where stream support is off.
The widget that reopens the document the user was last reading; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE.
S1401: keeps the installed-app cache used by the launch panel in step with installs, removals and locale changes, and is exported because the sender is the system.
S0134: the widget that shows the latest camera photos on the home screen; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE.
The widget that rotates a random photo on the home screen; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE.
S0134: the widget that starts a random track from the home screen; an AppWidget provider must be exported, and the photos flavor removes it because it ships no audio support.

The now-playing widget with its favourite toggle; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE and its own toggle action, and lite and photos remove it because neither ships persistent audio playback.
S0349: the one-tap voice-note widget; an AppWidget provider must be exported, and lite, photos and FOSS remove it because SUPPORT_MIC_RECORDING is false there.
S0369: the widget that captures a photo straight into a configured target; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE.
S0568: the config-less widget that opens the unified in-app camera; an AppWidget provider must be exported, and runtime degradation is handled by its trampoline rather than by manifest gating.
S0369: the per-widget target configuration screen the launcher starts with APPWIDGET_CONFIGURE, which requires an exported activity.
The calculator widget; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher.

S1411: the stopwatch widget, which also listens for BOOT_COMPLETED because the elapsed-realtime clock restarts at a reboot and nothing else would redraw a running cell; both senders are the system, so the receiver is exported.
The front-screen flashlight widget; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher.
S2516: the water flashlight widget; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher.
S3033: the tourist telemetry widget; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher.
The widget that opens camera OCR translation; an AppWidget provider must be exported, and lite, photos and FOSS remove it because ENABLE_TRANSLATION is false there.
The capture-and-OCR panel widget; an AppWidget provider must be exported, and lite, photos and FOSS remove it because ENABLE_TRANSLATION is false there.
The widget that launches the embedded game; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE from the launcher.
Reschedules scheduled file operations after a reboot and is exported because BOOT_COMPLETED comes from the system; the release build type ships it disabled while the feature is hidden from Play.
S2776: re-posts the flashlight shade shortcut after a reboot, because a notification does not survive one, and is exported because BOOT_COMPLETED comes from the system.

Restarts the playback service from cold when a headset media button is pressed; the MEDIA_BUTTON broadcast comes from the system, it is enabled only when the app is the primary media player, and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
S0380: the fallback direct-launch target for external media intents, kept exported so a file manager can still open a file with it when the per-type aliases are switched off.
S0422: imports a shared .fmsr resource file arriving by VIEW from a file manager or by SEND from the share sheet, both of which require an exported activity.
S0984: imports a companion .fmscfg SFTP-access file tapped in a messenger or shared to the app, which requires an exported activity; lite removes it because it has no SFTP support to configure.

The VIEW alias that makes the app openable as an audio player from file managers and share sheets, and eligible for the Android 10+ music role; it ships disabled and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
The VIEW alias that makes the app openable as a video player from file managers and share sheets; it ships disabled and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
The VIEW alias that makes the app openable as an image viewer from file managers and share sheets; it ships disabled and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
The VIEW alias that makes the app openable for PDF, EPUB and Office documents; it ships disabled and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
S0380: the VIEW alias for plain text, split out of the documents alias so text never loads the PDF and WebView stack; it ships disabled until the user makes the app a default handler.
S0380: the VIEW alias that uniquely owns typeless intents through a scheme-only filter and forwards them to the right specialised screen without adding a duplicate chooser entry; it ships disabled.
The SEND alias that puts the app in the system share sheet for audio files; a share target must be exported, it ships disabled, and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
The SEND alias that puts the app in the system share sheet for video files; a share target must be exported, it ships disabled, and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
The SEND alias that puts the app in the system share sheet for images; a share target must be exported, it ships disabled, and lite removes it with the rest of the default-player components.
The SEND alias that accepts plain text and links shared from browsers and social apps, writes them to a file and offers the copy-to dialog; a share target must be exported and it ships disabled.

S2920: exposes the Android 16+ Assistant Actions the system assistant calls; the service must be exported to be bound from outside and is guarded by BIND_APP_FUNCTION_SERVICE so only the platform may bind it.
S1440: the Network Monitor home-screen widget, declared only in the source set the two monitor-capable flavors mount, so the other flavors never merge a widget that could not work.
S1440: the APPWIDGET_CONFIGURE screen the launcher starts for the Network Monitor widget, declared beside the widget in the same monitor-only source set.
S1881: the Quick Settings tile that toggles the sideload build's silent-capture accessibility service; bound by the system and guarded by BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE.
S1881: the home-screen widget that toggles the same sideload-only accessibility capture; an AppWidget provider must be exported to receive APPWIDGET_UPDATE and its toggle action.

S0672: the Play-safe Quick Settings fallback that starts the MediaProjection capture path with no overlay and no special-use service; it is injected into standard only while the fms.edgeGestureTile gradle property is on, and that property is off in the current tree, so today the declaration reaches no flavor.
S0249: the dedicated OpenXR session host; exported so the HorizonOS launcher can discover its VR-category intent filter, although the app itself always starts it by explicit intent.

S0963: the immersive file browser host, which mirrors the diagnostic host's headset-mode intent filter and is exported for the same reason; it carries no launcher category, so it never appears in the app grid.

S0403/S1697: the GMS WearableListenerService that receives sync requests, playback state, favourites deltas and file channels from the watch; Google Play Services starts it from another process, so it must be exported.
S2881: the listen-to-the-watch widget, declared in the Wear overlay so flavors without the watch bridge never offer a widget that could not work; an AppWidget provider must be exported.
The watch app's launcher entry, exported so the Wear OS launcher can start it.

S2511: the Wear tile holding the mini-programs shortcut grid; the tile framework binds it from outside the process and it is guarded by BIND_TILE_PROVIDER, and it is one of only two components the Play variant declares (S3178).

S1697/S1861: the watch-side Data Layer listener that receives the phone's resource push, playback commands, settings and file channels; GMS starts it from another process, so it must be exported, and S3178 confines it to the sideload variant.

S1955: the Wear tile for the last network resource; bound by the tile framework and guarded by BIND_TILE_PROVIDER, and confined to the sideload variant because remote sources are outside the store boundary (S3178).
S1955: the Wear tile for saved streams; bound by the tile framework and guarded by BIND_TILE_PROVIDER, and confined to the sideload variant because streams are outside the store boundary (S3178).
S1955: the Wear tile for favourites; bound by the tile framework and guarded by BIND_TILE_PROVIDER, and confined to the sideload variant under the store boundary policy (S3178).

S2511: the Wear tile holding the home-sections shortcut grid; bound by the tile framework and guarded by BIND_TILE_PROVIDER, and confined to the sideload variant under the store boundary policy (S3178).

S2047: the watch-face complication showing the last used resource; the complication framework binds it from outside and it is guarded by BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER, and it is sideload-only under the store boundary policy (S3178).

S2047: the watch-face complication showing the favourites count; bound by the complication framework and guarded by BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER, and sideload-only under the store boundary policy (S3178).

S2047: the watch-face complication showing what is playing now; bound by the complication framework and guarded by BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER, and sideload-only under the store boundary policy (S3178).

S0565/S2498: points both apps at res/xml/network_security_config.xml, which permits cleartext app-wide because the user-supplied stream list is mostly plain-HTTP internet radio that a static allowlist cannot cover, and which trusts user-installed CAs for the cloud domains so MITM proxies do not break sign-in.

Lets the user's settings, resource list and favourites survive a device change through the platform backup, with the sensitive paths excluded by the two rule files below rather than by switching backup off wholesale.

Names res/xml/backup_rules.xml, which keeps the encrypted credentials database and the settings DataStore out of cloud backup on API 30 and below, because their keys are bound to this device's hardware keystore and cannot be restored anywhere else.

S1552: names res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml, which from API 31 supersedes the backup rules for both cloud backup and device-to-device transfer and must repeat every exclusion, or the credentials database and settings DataStore are silently backed up on every modern device.

S0349/S1862/S3154: types every service that owns a live microphone session outside a screen - the Quick Audio Recorder, the live broadcast capture, and the watch's voice recorder, which must keep recording after the wrist drops.
S3154: only the sideload build keeps the camera broadcasting after the app leaves the screen, so only its copy of VideoBroadcastService carries the camera type; the store copy is declared without it.

Types background audio playback on both devices, the SOS siren that must survive its window being destroyed (S3216), and the WorkManager foreground service; from API 34 Media3 demands this type on any playback start.
Types the WorkManager foreground service while it runs scheduled file operations on Android 14+, alongside the mediaPlayback type the same service needs for audio work.

S3558: the provider behind slot 2 of the FastMediaSorter watch face, serving the shortcut, app value or system value the phone companion chose for that slot; bound by the complication framework and guarded by BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER, and sideload-only under the store boundary policy (S3178) because the choice arrives over the Data Layer listener that only the noLegal watch build declares.
